core_constraint: Required engine labs use Python standard-library facilities and NumPy array primitives. High-level ML frameworks may appear only in optional comparison work after the from-scratch checkpoint passes.
completion_policy: A module completes only when its artifact, automated checks, explanation, and safety gates pass. Reading or video completion alone is never sufficient.

tracks.title: Launch Pad: Python, Workspaces, and Git
tracks.summary: Build the programming and version-control habits needed to work safely inside Daedalus.

modules.title: Python Workbench
modules.summary: Use functions, data structures, exceptions, paths, isolated environments, and tests to build a small engineering tool.
objectives: Read and write small Python modules with explicit functions and a main entry point.
Create an isolated environment and explain why it protects unrelated projects.
Use pathlib without string-built paths and report actionable exceptions.
Write deterministic unit tests for normal, edge, and failure cases.

lab.title: CLI engineering calculator
instructions: Accept two numeric values and a named operation.
Separate parsing, calculation, and presentation functions.
Reject invalid numbers and unsupported operations with a short explanation.
Test success, zero, negative, and invalid-input cases.
lab.deliverable: A tested Python module that can run from a fresh isolated environment.

checks: Fresh environment imports the module without global packages.
Automated test discovery passes.
Invalid input exits nonzero without a traceback dump to a beginner.
No file operation escapes its supplied temporary directory.

modules.title: Git Without Accidental Publication
modules.summary: Understand the working tree, staging index, commits, branches, remotes, and ignore limits before automating a push.
objectives: Distinguish working-tree, staged, committed, ignored, and untracked content.
Create a focused branch, inspect a staged diff, commit, and merge it.
Explain why .gitignore does not remove already tracked files.
Resolve a remote-ahead situation without defaulting to force push.

lab.title: Publication-state fixture
instructions: Create a disposable repository with public source and a fake private output.
Observe the path before and after an ignore rule.
Stage it deliberately, add the rule, and prove it remains tracked.
Remove it from the proposed commit while preserving the working copy.
lab.deliverable: A command transcript explaining each Git state and the non-destructive remediation.

checks: Learner identifies the exact staged snapshot before committing.
Tracked-versus-ignored behavior is demonstrated correctly.
A branch and merge preserve both intended changes.
No force-push command is used in the conflict exercise.

tracks.title: Math Forge: The Mathematics Used by Learning Systems
tracks.summary: Connect geometry, derivatives, probability, and floating-point behavior to code and diagnostics.

modules.title: Vectors, Matrices, and Linear Transforms
modules.summary: Model features, batches, and learned affine layers with explicit shapes and linear algebra.
objectives: Compute dot products, matrix products, transposes, norms, and affine transforms by hand for small cases.
Interpret rows, columns, samples, features, inputs, and outputs consistently.
Use least squares as a reference solution for linear regression.
Predict the output shape of vector, matrix, and batched matrix products.

lab.title: Affine transformation explorer
instructions: Represent three two-feature samples as a matrix.
Apply a hand-selected weight matrix and bias.
Calculate one output manually and compare every output with NumPy.
Change one shape incorrectly and explain the resulting contract failure.
lab.deliverable: A shape-annotated calculation with manual and NumPy results.

checks: Manual products agree with NumPy within 1e-12 in float64.
Every axis has a written semantic label.
Least-squares oracle is used without computing an explicit matrix inverse.
Incompatible inner dimensions are explained before execution.

modules.title: Derivatives, Chain Rule, and Uncertainty
modules.summary: Develop the derivative and probability concepts needed for loss optimization and honest evaluation.
objectives: Interpret a derivative as local sensitivity and calculate common derivative rules.
Compose sensitivities with the chain rule.
Explain gradient and Jacobian roles without materializing unnecessary full Jacobians.
Use random variables, mean, variance, and sampling to describe experiment uncertainty.

lab.title: Finite-difference sensitivity lab
instructions: Choose a smooth composed scalar function.
Derive its gradient using local rules and the chain rule.
Compute centered finite differences across several epsilon values.
Repeat a seeded noisy estimate and summarize mean and variance.
lab.deliverable: A derivative comparison table and a short uncertainty explanation.

checks: Centered finite-difference relative error is below 1e-6 for smooth fixtures.
Chain-rule factor order and shapes are correct.
Random experiment records seed, sample count, mean, and variance.
Learner distinguishes observed sample variation from a deterministic implementation bug.

modules.title: Floating-Point Range and Stable Formulas
modules.summary: Recognize overflow, underflow, cancellation, invalid domains, and dtype-dependent behavior.
objectives: Explain how dtype changes precision, range, and memory.
Locate the first non-finite operation with finite-value summaries.
Implement stable softmax and stable log-loss calculations.
Choose tolerances that match the dtype and operation scale.

lab.title: Extreme-logit laboratory
instructions: Evaluate naive exponential normalization at increasing scales.
Record where overflow first appears for float32 and float64.
Implement maximum-shifted softmax along a named class axis.
Verify finite outputs and row sums for logits [-1000, 0, 1000].
lab.deliverable: A stable softmax implementation and diagnostic trace for the naive failure.

checks: Extreme-logit outputs are finite and sum to one within 1e-12 in float64.
Maximum is reduced along the documented class axis with keepdims.
Invalid log and divide domains raise or report a typed cause.
No global warning suppression or NaN-to-zero masking is used.

tracks.title: Array Lab: NumPy Tensor Mechanics
tracks.summary: Master array shape, dtype, memory, vectorization, broadcasting, and reproducible random generation.

modules.title: Arrays, Axes, Dtypes, Views, and Broadcasting
modules.summary: Replace accidental loops and trial reshapes with explicit array contracts.
objectives: Create, index, reshape, transpose, aggregate, and vectorize arrays intentionally.
Distinguish a view from an independent copy.
Predict broadcasting compatibility by trailing-axis comparison.
Select and preserve a suitable numeric dtype.

lab.title: Loop-to-array translation
instructions: Implement a small feature normalization with explicit loops as an oracle.
Translate it to vectorized NumPy operations.
Test view/copy behavior with shares_memory.
Add compatible and incompatible broadcast fixtures.
lab.deliverable: A tested vectorized implementation with a shape contract table.

checks: Loop oracle and vectorized result agree with rtol 1e-7 and atol 1e-9 in float64.
View mutation behavior is predicted and tested.
Broadcast fixtures name expanded axes.
No flatten-or-tile workaround hides an incompatible model shape.

modules.title: Shape, Parameter, and Memory Calculators
modules.summary: Calculate model dimensions and memory before allocating arrays or starting a run.
objectives: Compute element counts and bytes from shape and dtype.
Count dense-layer weights and biases exactly.
Separate parameter, gradient, optimizer-state, and activation memory.
Record explicit RNG objects and environment versions for reproducibility.

lab.title: Architecture preflight
instructions: Describe a three-layer dense network and a batch shape.
Calculate parameter and activation elements by component.
Apply dtype item size and selected optimizer-state multipliers.
Allocate controlled arrays and compare estimates with nbytes.
lab.deliverable: An itemized preflight report with assumptions and exact controlled-case verification.

checks: Parameter count matches the actual model registry exactly.
Controlled allocation byte estimate equals summed ndarray.nbytes.
Transient and implementation overhead are labeled rather than promised exact.
Run record includes seed plus Python and NumPy versions.

tracks.title: Learning Fundamentals: Models Before Networks
tracks.summary: Build regression and classification from equations while keeping evaluation honest.

modules.title: Data Splits, Scaling, Metrics, and Leakage
modules.summary: Design experiments whose reported performance answers the intended question.
objectives: Separate training, validation, and test roles.
Fit preprocessing statistics on training data only.
Choose metrics that match regression or classification behavior.
Detect leakage, overfitting, and misleading aggregate results.

lab.title: Leakage demonstration
instructions: Create a fixed synthetic dataset and split before fitting any transform.
Compare a correct training-only scaler with an intentionally leaky scaler.
Train the same simple model under both conditions.
Explain why the leaky result is not admissible evidence.
lab.deliverable: A split manifest, metric report, and leakage audit.

checks: Split occurs before fitted preprocessing.
Data hashes or stable identifiers record which samples belong to each split.
Test set is not used for hyperparameter selection.
Training and validation curves are interpreted separately.

modules.title: Linear and Logistic Learners
modules.summary: Implement supervised prediction, loss, analytical gradients, and optimization without an ML framework.
objectives: Implement linear regression with mean-squared error.
Implement binary logistic prediction and a stable classification loss.
Derive parameter gradients and verify them numerically.
Compare a learned linear solution to a trustworthy NumPy oracle.

lab.title: First Learner
instructions: Fit seeded y = 3x + 2 + noise data.
Record the loss and parameter trajectory.
Compare gradients to centered finite differences.
Compare final parameters with least squares.
lab.deliverable: A reproducible regression report and a tested binary classifier.

checks: Analytical gradients have relative error below 1e-6 on fixed fixtures.
Regression recovers known parameters within declared noise-aware tolerance.
Classifier reaches at least 95 percent on a deliberately separable fixed set.
Stable loss remains finite for extreme logits.

tracks.title: Autograd Foundry: Reverse-Mode Differentiation
tracks.summary: Build the graph and backward engine that make every neural-network primitive inspectable.

modules.title: Scalar Computation Tape
modules.summary: Learn reverse accumulation on a minimal graph before adding array shape complexity.
objectives: Record operation parents and local backward rules.
Produce a reverse topological traversal.
Accumulate contributions at graph branches.
Define gradient reset, detach, and repeated-backward behavior.

lab.title: Derivative Detective scalar graph
instructions: Implement scalar add, multiply, power, exp, log, and ReLU nodes.
Seed a scalar output gradient and walk the graph backward.
Trace x*x + x to prove branch accumulation.
Compare each leaf gradient with centered finite differences.
lab.deliverable: A scalar autograd module, graph trace, and gradient-check suite.

checks: Each reachable node is visited after its consumers.
Branch contributions are summed exactly once.
Smooth gradient relative error is below 1e-6 in float64.
Invalid domains and graph lifecycle violations are typed.

modules.title: NumPy Tensor Autograd
modules.summary: Extend reverse mode to shaped arrays, reductions, matrix products, and broadcasting.
objectives: Implement array-valued add, subtract, multiply, divide, power, reshape, transpose, sum, mean, matmul, and ReLU.
Propagate vector-Jacobian products without materializing full Jacobians.
Reduce broadcast gradients exactly to each input shape.
Gradient-check scalar, elementwise, reduction, and matrix operations.

lab.title: Tensor primitive matrix
instructions: Create fixtures spanning scalar, vector, matrix, and batched shapes.
Test every forward result against direct NumPy.
Test every backward result with centered finite differences.
Include bias broadcasting and multiple-path graphs.
lab.deliverable: A Tensor API with a parameterized primitive and gradient-check suite.

checks: Relative gradient error is below 1e-5 across required operations.
Every stored gradient exactly matches its tensor shape.
Bias and multi-axis broadcast gradients use sum-to-shape semantics.
No object dtype or implicit arbitrary-code serialization enters the engine.

tracks.title: Neural Workshop: Layers, Losses, and Training
tracks.summary: Assemble tested primitives into reusable models, optimizers, training loops, diagnostics, and checkpoints.

modules.title: Modules, Parameters, Activations, and Losses
modules.summary: Create composable trainable layers with explicit state and stable objectives.
objectives: Register each trainable parameter exactly once.
Implement Linear, ReLU, sigmoid, tanh, and stable softmax behavior.
Implement MSE and cross-entropy with documented reduction semantics.
Verify forward shape and backward gradient contracts per layer.

lab.title: Layer assembly bench
instructions: Build Linear-ReLU-Linear as a sequential model.
List parameters, shapes, dtypes, and exact counts.
Run a fixed batch through each activation and loss.
Gradient-check every trainable layer and objective.
lab.deliverable: A composable model and layer contract report.

checks: Parameter registry has no duplicates or missing trainable arrays.
Forward output shapes match declared contracts.
Stable cross-entropy remains finite for extreme logits.
Layer and loss gradient relative error is below 1e-5.

modules.title: Optimizers, Mini-Batches, and Trainer State
modules.summary: Turn gradients into controlled, reproducible parameter updates.
objectives: Implement SGD, Momentum, and Adam from their update equations.
Define zeroing, accumulation, optimizer-step, and train/eval order.
Shuffle and batch data through an explicit Generator.
Record configuration, versions, metrics, and stop reason for every run.

lab.title: XOR optimizer ladder
instructions: Preserve a one-linear-layer XOR failure as a baseline.
Train a hidden-layer model with SGD.
Hand-calculate one Momentum and Adam update and compare code.
Run the fixed-seed experiment and record metrics.
lab.deliverable: An optimizer equation test suite and deterministic XOR run.

checks: One-step optimizer fixtures match hand-computed values.
Bias correction and state initialization are verified for Adam.
Fixed-seed multilayer model classifies all four XOR inputs.
Run metadata contains seed, versions, data identity, and complete hyperparameters.

modules.title: Gradient Health and Safe Checkpoints
modules.summary: Observe failures early and persist numeric state without executable object formats.
objectives: Track loss, parameter norms, gradient norms, non-finite counts, latency, and throughput.
Distinguish an optimization symptom from an incorrect derivative.
Save named arrays with validated JSON metadata and checksums.
Reject object arrays, shape mismatch, tampering, and untrusted pickle.

lab.title: Fault injection and checkpoint round-trip
instructions: Inject an excessive learning rate and locate the first unhealthy signal.
Restore the correct rate and overfit a fixed 32-example sanity batch.
Save arrays and metadata, then reload into a fresh matching model.
Modify the archive and verify checksum rejection.
lab.deliverable: A diagnostic timeline and tamper-detecting checkpoint fixture.

checks: First non-finite operation is reported with redacted numeric evidence.
Sanity batch reaches the declared overfit target before larger training.
Checkpoint arrays round-trip with np.array_equal.
allow_pickle is false and tampered archives fail closed.

tracks.title: Deep Architecture Lab
tracks.summary: Implement convolution, normalization, dropout, attention, and transformer blocks from inspectable primitives.

modules.title: Convolution, Normalization, and Dropout
modules.summary: Add spatial parameter sharing and stateful train/eval operations without hiding shape or gradient logic.
objectives: Implement a slow, clear convolution oracle and a vectorized equivalent.
Derive input, kernel, and bias gradients.
Implement normalization with explicit training and evaluation state.
Implement inverted dropout using an explicit random Generator.

lab.title: Signal-kernel laboratory
instructions: Convolve a small one-dimensional signal by hand and with a loop oracle.
Implement the vectorized forward path.
Gradient-check input, kernel, and bias.
Verify normalization and dropout state differences.
lab.deliverable: Tested convolution, normalization, and dropout primitives with state documentation.

checks: Vectorized convolution output matches the loop oracle.
All convolution gradients pass below 1e-5 relative error.
Evaluation normalization uses recorded statistics rather than the current batch.
Dropout is disabled in evaluation and reproducible with recorded training RNG state.

modules.title: Attention and a Tiny Transformer
modules.summary: Build the core sequence-modeling block and inspect its masking, probabilities, gradients, and memory.
objectives: Implement embeddings, scaled dot-product attention, and causal masking.
Explain query, key, value, sequence, head, and feature axes.
Assemble residual, normalization, and feed-forward paths.
Measure attention memory growth with sequence length.

lab.title: One-block character transformer
instructions: Create a deterministic character vocabulary and next-token batches.
Implement one attention head and its causal mask.
Add the feed-forward and residual block.
Overfit one batch before training a small local corpus.
lab.deliverable: A tiny character transformer with attention inspection and deterministic generation.

checks: Attention rows are finite and sum to one.
Every future-token probability is zero under the causal mask.
Primitive gradients pass targeted finite-difference checks.
Fixed-corpus loss falls at least 50 percent and the recorded run can be replayed.

tracks.title: Daedalus Systems Lab: Operator Workflows
tracks.summary: Turn educational primitives into a local-first workbench with strict private-data boundaries and recoverable state.

modules.title: Private Workspaces and the Constrained Runner
modules.summary: Keep learner projects separate from public source and run ordinary learning code with bounded process controls.
objectives: Resolve and validate paths beneath a marked private workspace.
Reject traversal, wrong roots, symlink escapes, and unsupported file types.
Run Python with bounded time, output, working directory, and a minimal environment.
Explain why these controls are not a hostile-code sandbox.

lab.title: Boundary and timeout exercise
instructions: Create a marked temporary workspace outside a temporary source tree.
Run a small Python file within the projects directory.
Attempt parent traversal, an outside path, a blocked import, and an infinite loop.
Record deterministic stop reasons without leaking private absolute paths.
lab.deliverable: A path-policy and runner test suite plus an operator-facing boundary explanation.

checks: Source and workspace roots cannot contain one another.
Traversal and resolved outside paths fail closed.
Timeout and restricted-import fixtures stop cleanly.
Documentation directs hostile samples to a disposable VM.

modules.title: Operator UI, Run Registry, Backup, and Restore
modules.summary: Expose engine state without coupling the engine to the interface, and prove that private work can be recovered.
objectives: Keep UI actions behind small service interfaces with testable inputs and results.
Store run metadata separately from large arrays and private datasets.
Perform non-destructive backup to a marked external destination.
Restore to a new directory and verify expected file hashes.

lab.title: Vertical slice and restore drill
instructions: Create a project through the workspace service and open it in the file tree.
Run Shape Detective and persist its redacted run metadata.
Back up source and private workspace to a marked temporary destination.
Restore the workspace to a new path and compare file hashes.
lab.deliverable: A thin project-calculator-run-backup workflow with a restore report.

checks: UI does not import private project content into the public source tree.
Backup refuses an unmarked nonempty destination.
Backup does not delete destination-only files after local deletion.
Restore never overwrites the active workspace and expected hashes match.

tracks.title: Secure Delivery: GitHub, Supply Chain, and Open Source
tracks.summary: Build a guarded publication and release process that reports evidence, fails safely, and never assumes automation is infallible.

modules.title: Push Guard and Dependency Findings
modules.summary: Inspect exact outgoing content for privacy, secrets, test failures, and dependency advisories before any network action.
objectives: Identify the exact outgoing commit range and changed files.
Distinguish local dependency audit results from authenticated GitHub Dependabot alerts.
Redact sensitive evidence and provide reversible remediation.
Block policy-threshold findings without force push or silent rewriting.

lab.title: Push Guardian fixture suite
instructions: Create clean, fake-secret, ignored-tracked, failing-test, and advisory fixtures.
Run a dry scan against the exact proposed publication set.
Verify deterministic finding IDs, severity, source, and safe action.
Confirm the clean fixture passes and unsafe fixtures block.
lab.deliverable: A redacted JSON and human-readable release-guard report.

checks: Report contains no fake secret value or private absolute path.
Ignored-but-tracked and non-fast-forward cases explain safe next steps.
No-patch advisory never claims an automatic fix.
No commit, push, alert dismissal, or dependency rewrite occurs in dry-run mode.

modules.title: CI, SBOM, Packaging, and Release Risk
modules.summary: Produce installable, attributable artifacts with test, dependency, integrity, and risk evidence.
objectives: Build source and wheel artifacts from declared project metadata.
Run tests and static checks in repeatable CI jobs.
Attach artifact checksums and a build-matched dependency inventory.
Apply NIST SSDF and AI RMF questions to release readiness.

lab.title: Release candidate rehearsal
instructions: Build artifacts from a clean checkout and locked environment.
Install the wheel into a fresh environment and launch a smoke test.
Generate checksums and dependency inventory for those exact artifacts.
Complete a release risk record with owner, evidence, exceptions, and rollback.
lab.deliverable: A release candidate folder and signed-off readiness checklist without publishing it.

checks: Fresh-environment install and smoke test pass.
CI covers supported Python and target Windows configurations.
Checksums and inventory correspond to the final artifacts.
Open blocking findings stop release; exceptions are explicit, owned, and time-bounded.

tracks.title: Capstone: From Equation to Installable Tool
tracks.summary: Integrate a transparent model, educational diagnostics, private workspace, recovery, and guarded release evidence.

modules.title: Auditable AI System Capstone
modules.summary: Choose a tabular classifier, small signal classifier, character transformer, or release-and-backup appliance and ship a complete local artifact.
objectives: State the problem, data boundary, metric, threat model, and non-goals.
Implement the required core behavior from NumPy primitives with numerical tests.
Expose diagnostics that explain shapes, gradients, training state, and failure modes.
Demonstrate reproducible install, private workspace handling, backup restore, and guarded release.

lab.title: Capstone build and defense
instructions: Submit a short design record and acceptance matrix before implementation.
Build the smallest vertical slice and pass numerical gates before UI expansion.
Run fault, privacy, restore, and clean-install drills.
Present evidence and explain one limitation in each of correctness, security, and generalization.
lab.deliverable: An installable local project, tests, operator guide, learning explanation, and release evidence bundle.

checks: Numerical correctness contributes 30 percent and all hard numeric gates pass.
Tests and diagnostics contribute 20 percent; explainability 15 percent; reproducibility 10 percent.
Security and privacy contribute 10 percent; packaging and UX 10 percent; attribution 5 percent.
Overall score is at least 80 percent with zero failed hard security or recovery gates.
